parts.name: Arrival
parts.stand: Outside the market building, at the edge of the old town.

paras.t: This is Chania's Municipal Market, the Agora. It's an indoor market from 1913, right on the edge of the old town, and locals use it as much as visitors do. It was renovated in 2026, this very year.

1913 is a telling date. From 1898 to 1913, Chania was the capital of the Cretan State, a semi-autonomous Crete, and many important buildings went up in those years. Then, on 1 December 1913, Crete was united with Greece. So this market belongs to the very end of that era.

The square out here, the Market Square, is one of the largest central squares in town. And there's history underneath: mosaics from Late Roman houses, signs of a prosperous city, were found near Agora Square.

parts.name: Inside
parts.stand: Step inside, out of the sun.

paras.t: I'll be honest with you: my sources don't describe the stalls or the building in any detail, so let your eyes, and your nose, lead you. What I can tell you is what this region grows: olives and olive oil, citrus, wine, avocados, dairy, and honey. See how many you can find.
Ask before you photograph a stallholder, and keep an eye on your bag when it gets crowded.

parts.name: Before you go
parts.stand: Wherever you like inside the market.

paras.t: A market is where a town shows you what it eats and how it talks. Buy something small, take your time, and listen for a minute before you move on.
